findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional mutable-buffer two-pointer solution. Its vowel set handles both cases, left and right skip only fixed non-vowels, each swap reverses one outer vowel pair, and joining once avoids repeated string copies. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 345 and its Python reverseVowels surface. The Reference preserves vowel-only reversal, case sensitivity, fixed non-vowel positions, both source examples and the first explanation, and both source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064516450. Its vowel set, mutable conversion, pointer scans, paired swap, inward updates, and final join are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the required Solution wrapper.

The legal all-vowel tiers use 1,024, 8,192, and 65,536 characters, span 64x, and force every position into the reversal. The current source passes all nine executions at -0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; a correct front-inserted vowel stack passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +0.30 and 5.44x.

The Approach accurately derives outermost-vowel pairing, proves fixed non-vowel positions and reversed vowel order, traces the mixed-case source example, and states O(n) time with O(n) Python string-buffer space.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, the first source explanation, the ten upper- and lowercase vowels, and both length and printable-ASCII constraints.
